newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real falls 0.18 pct on dollar outflows.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real falls 0.18 pct on dollar outflows.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.18 percent to close at 1.0765 per dollar on Thursday due to dollar outflows in the commercial foreign exchange market and a decline in the real-dollar mini-band, dealers said.
At 1645 local/1945 GMT, preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts showed a $150 million deficit.
The real's fall was also due to a 0.14 percent lowering of the mini-band by the Central Bank to between 1.0745 and 1.0795 reais per dollar.
The previous mini-band was set on June 12 at between 1.0730 and 1.0780 per dollar.
So far this month, the mini-band has fallen 0.42 percent against the dollar compared to monthly declines of between 0.57 and 0.63 percent in the past six months.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0793 per dollar, down 0.07 percent.
In the parallel market, the real dropped 0.44 percent to end at 1.138 per dollar due to a reduction in the supply of dollars, traders said.
